gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-serif-h: Early GameBoy strides out with wide tracking and a skyward x-height, playful and commanding. Noto Serif Hentaigana does the quieter work, its open-jawed curves and subtly modulated strokes suited to steady reading.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-ovo: Loud and loose, Early GameBoy strides across the line with widely spaced letters and a skyward x-height. Ovo keeps its thins only slightly lighter than its thicks, with generous gaps at curve terminals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-esteban: Edo SZ draws lowercase letters with the stature of cast iron capitals, all in one constant stroke width. Esteban takes over with lightly shaded texture running through each word.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-faustina: Every Edo SZ letter looks outlined with one steady thickness, like a technical drawing pen. Faustina counters with gently thinning bowls, and that pull between uniform line and soft shading is what lingers.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Edo SZ keeps one constant stroke width, like outlines drawn with a single pen. Hedvig Letters Serif handles the finer work, with open curves and crossbars a bit slimmer than its stems.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-lisu-bosa: Words read sturdy and large here, with counters spilling into the surrounding space and softly thinned curves on top. Lisu Bosa handles the reading, while Edo SZ does the shouting in a single drawing-pen line weight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-serif-hentaiga: Noto Serif Hentaigana reads with open jaws on every curve and modest stroke modulation, its small letters nearly matching capitals in height. Under Edo SZ's uniform lines, a long text would glide along smoothly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-ovo: Ovo offers a gentle modulation and spacious curve terminals that keep paragraphs comfortable. Beside Edo SZ, whose curves meet stems without any swelling, that softness becomes the pair's real strength.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-esteban: Eight Bit Dragon strides along in widely separated letters with a towering lowercase. Esteban does the quieter job, its barely thinned strokes and an e that never looks squeezed shut keeping text comfortable.
